query: For an FCC/BCC high-entropy-alloy protective coating susceptible to progressive plastic deformation during continuous loading, what testable mechanistic hypothesis could explain its creep resistance? Specify the governing factor and rationale, an unspecified controlled comparison that would reveal it, predicted observations relative to the starting baseline, the operating boundaries under sustained stress, supporting prior evidence, and a clear falsification criterion.

generation.hypothesis: In FCC/BCC high-entropy protective coatings, the intrinsic creep resistance under sustained plastic loading is primarily due to the development of a rafted microstructure at the coherent FCC/BCC interfaces. This raft formation, driven by a positive lattice misfit and sustained stress at elevated temperatures, impedes dislocation climb and motion, thereby slowing creep deformation.
generation.material_initial_state: A homogeneous protective coating with a random distribution of an FCC matrix and dispersed BCC precipitates.
generation.intervention: Apply a controlled heat treatment and sustained mechanical loading (within service-relevant temperature and stress bounds) to induce directional microstructural evolution (i.e., rafting) versus a comparably processed control sample in which the rafting is suppressed.
generation.conditions: Elevated temperatures and continuous loading conditions representative of service environments, maintained long enough for possible rafting of the BCC phase to occur (operating boundaries defined by temperatures that allow diffusion without causing phase instability or coarsening).
generation.structural_mediator: The formation of a parallel rafted structure at the FCC/BCC interfaces that creates coherent, strain-bearing barriers to dislocation climb.
generation.mechanism: Positive lattice misfit between the FCC matrix and BCC precipitates promotes rafting under sustained stress. This new microstructural arrangement increases the barriers for dislocation climb by both enhancing local coherency strains and reducing the effective diffusion paths, which slows the rate of plastic deformation (creep).
generation.predicted_outcome: Samples in which rafting is induced will exhibit a lower creep strain rate and delayed onset of tertiary creep compared to baseline samples with a random phase distribution. Microstructural analysis should reveal aligned (rafted) BCC precipitates and associated dislocation configurations that indicate impeded climb.
generation.baseline: The initial state of the coating with a uniform, randomly distributed FCC and BCC microstructure that has not undergone directional rafting.
generation.boundary: The hypothesis is expected to hold under sustained loading conditions at temperatures high enough to permit interfacial diffusion and rafting but below those that would cause deleterious phase coarsening or a complete transformation of the microstructure.
generation.uncertainty: The precise dependence of the raft formation kinetics on stress magnitude, temperature, and BCC phase volume fraction remains to be quantified. Additionally, variations in coherency strain may alter the effectiveness of the rafted structure in impeding dislocation motion.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of identical FCC/BCC HEA protective coating samples. One set will be subjected to a pre-treatment protocol (controlled heat therapy plus sustained uniaxial stress) designed to induce rafting, while the control set will be processed to maintain a random phase distribution. Both sets will then be exposed to long-term creep testing at a temperature and stress level chosen to activate creep mechanisms without triggering full phase transformation.
measurements: Measure creep strain versus time for both sample sets using high-precision extensometry.
Characterize and quantify the microstructural state (e.g., raft formation, interphase spacing, dislocation density) using TEM/SEM imaging before and after creep testing.
Determine the creep rate exponents and activation energies from deformation data.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If samples with the induced raft microstructure do not display a statistically significant reduction in creep strain rate or delayed tertiary creep compared to the control samples, or if microstructural analyses do not reveal the predicted raft formation, then the hypothesis that rafting at coherent FCC/BCC interfaces governs the enhanced creep resistance is falsified.

cited_evidence.text: Abstract This article presents the high temperature tensile and creep behaviors of a novel high entropy alloy (HEA). The microstructure of this HEA resembles that of advanced superalloys with a high entropy FCC matrix and L1 2 ordered precipitates, so it is also named as “high entropy superalloy (HESA)”. The tensile yield strengths of HESA surpass those of the reported HEAs from room temperature to elevated temperatures; furthermore, its creep resistance at 982 °C can be compared to those of some Ni-based superalloys. Analysis on experimental results indicate that HESA could be strengthened by the low stacking-fault energy of the matrix, high anti-phase boundary energy of the strengthening precipitate, and thermally stable microstructure. Positive misfit between FCC matrix and precipitate has yielded parallel raft microstructure during creep at 982 °C, and the creep curves of HESA were dominated by tertiary creep behavior. To the best of authors’ knowledge, this article is the first to present the elevated temperature tensile creep study on full scale specimens of a high entropy alloy, and the potential of HESA for high temperature structural application is discussed.

Contrary to LSR, creep deformation in HSR exhibits abnormally high stress exponents of 8.9–14 and an average activation energy of 380 kJ mol −1 . Combined with the dislocation configurations in Figure 8 c and Figure 9 c, the same creep mechanism may also be considered rate-controlling. The unusually high stress exponents and activation energy in several traditional alloys have been frequently described using the power-law breakdown equation [ [43] , [44] , [45] , [46] ]. However, no deviation from the linear relationship on double-logarithmic curves of log ε ˙ ~ log σ were observed, and therefore, the power-law breakdown assumption may be inappropriate for the present alloy.
